$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: the run added the evaluation-pr job and left the job the earlier run wrote beside it. Two jobs now carry the plan's marker and run the pr tier, which the re-render rule exists to prevent.
The new job is the capture's and the stale job is the pipeline's own, so the result is the two elements the stale job breaks.
derivation: The file parses and lints clean. Two jobs carry the marker and two jobs run the pr tier's command, so the evaluation-pr job element misses (it expects one job for the tier), and the stale job holds the pr tier step under a name that lists two of the four checks, so the tier step element misses too; every other element is present.

elementMisses: command-evaluation-ci-pr: the step that runs npm exec --prefix evals -- tea-evaluate ci --evaluation evals/ledger --tier pr is not named for seal, replay
job-evaluation-pr: 2 job(s) run npm exec --prefix evals -- tea-evaluate ci --evaluation evals/ledger --tier pr (evaluation-pr, evaluation-evals-ledger-pr), expected 1
